classification.description: Doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium)

origin_result.basis: Origin check status is INSUFFICIENT_DATA; missing a bill of materials (each input's description, 6-digit HS code, origin country, value and currency) and a declaration (product price, FOB or Ex-Works basis, final manufacture in the UAE, operations done in the UAE).

procedure.step: Register the factory with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism (must be outside a free zone, with a MoIAT industrial licence and a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added); processing takes about 3 working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: Log in to the ministry e-services portal, choose the Certificate of Origin for India service, fill in the application form, upload the required documents (proof of factory registration, commercial invoice, and for a trading exporter the factory's purchase invoice), pay the fee online, submit the application, and print the approved certificate.
Certificate of Origin fee: AED 10 to AED 200 (fee range because shipment value is not given).

The certificate is valid for 12 months from the date of issue, covers only one import, and must be issued before, at, or within 5 working days of export; it must bear the authorised signature and official seal of the competent authority.
Ship the goods directly from the UAE to India; transit through another country is allowed only under customs control, with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry, holds origin information including which origin criterion is claimed, and keeps supporting documents for at least 5 years from the date of filing; electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to e-Sanchit (unconfirmed).
The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least 5 years starting from the end of the calendar year of the certificate's issue.

caveats.note: Mansha interprets '+' in the rule as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+'.
Direct labour cost and direct overhead cost are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
De minimis tolerance helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the value-addition percentage.
The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty only; IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge, and any anti-dumping or safeguard duties still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
Certificate fee bands are in AED and apply to the invoice value in AED; no currency conversion is done by Mansha.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is a prerequisite for the certificate; confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
India's certificate form uses box 9 for remarks, while the agreement text says box 8; India's form governs entry into India.
Electronic certificate acceptance and upload to India's e-Sanchit system comes from CBIC Instruction 28/2022, which Mansha has read only through secondary reports.
UAE law sets a 3-year record-keeping minimum, but the CEPA's 5-year requirement governs CEPA claims.
